  411 W. OCEAN BOULEVARD

Mary Zendejas, 1st District  Megan Kerr, 5th District
Cindy Allen, 2nd District  Dr. Suely Saro, 6th District

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

 NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC
 The consent calendar shall be heard immediately after the pledge of allegiance, and prior to 6:30
 PM. All matters listed under the Consent Calendar are to be considered routine by the City Council
 and will all be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate discussion of said items unless the
 Mayor, City Councilmembers or the City Manager request specific items be discussed and/or
 removed from the Consent Calendar for separate action.

 CONSENT CALENDAR (1 – 23)

 1.  25-56604  Recommendation to increase appropriations in the General Fund Group in the City
  Manager Department by $8,100, offset by the Second Council District One-Time
  District Priority Funds, transferred from the Citywide Activities Department, to
  provide contributions of:
  • $750 to the Long Beach Restaurant Association for their 2025 Cruisin’ For A
  Cause fundraiser at Anchors Away Boat Rentals on September 14, 2025;
  • $100 to Creative Art Events Inc. for the 2nd Annual Trashion Show Long
  Beach on September 21, 2025;
  • $500 to Long Beach Public Library Foundation for their 22nd Annual Grape
  Expectations Gala on September 28, 2025;
  • $500 to Long Beach Century Club for the Long Beach Mayor’s Trophy
  Charity Golf Tournament on September 11, 2024;
  • $5,500 to International City Theatre for their Encore 40th Anniversary
  Celebration on October 8, 2025;
  • $500 to the Office of Special Events and Filming for the 4th Annual Filipino
  American History Month Celebration on October 7, 2025;

  Page 1 of 12

  Fundraiser on October 4, 2025; and

  Decrease appropriations in the General Fund Group in the Citywide Activities
  Department by $8,100, to offset a transfer to the City Manager Department.

  Office or Department:  Cindy Allen, Councilwoman, Second District

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

  Manager Department by $775, offset by the Sixth Council District One-Time

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

  one-year periods, at the discretion of the City Manager; and, authorize City

  Increase appropriations in the Fleet Services Fund Group in the Financial

PUBLIC COMMENT: OBTAIN SPEAKER CARD FROM THE CITY CLERK
Opportunity to address the City Council (on non-agenda items) is given to the first 10 persons who
submit Speaker Cards to the City Clerk beginning at 15 minutes prior to the commencement of the
meeting. Each speaker is allowed three minutes to make their comments.

REGULAR AGENDA

24. 25-56605  Recommendation to request City Manager to return to Long Beach City Council by
  the October 21, 2025, City Council meeting with a status update presentation on
  the residential organics (green cart) collection program and a detailed plan to
  address the ongoing constituent concerns related to missed collections, availability
  of carts for exchange requests, and customer service satisfaction.

  Office or Department:  Daryl Supernaw, Councilman, Fourth District

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

25. 25-56613  Recommendation to request City Attorney to agendize an ordinance to regulate the
  sale and use of CA State Fire Marshall-approved ground-based sparkling devices

  Page 7 of 12
   CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
  TUESDAY, OCTOBER 7, 2025
  411 W. OCEAN BOULEVARD
  CIVIC CHAMBERS, 5:00 PM

  (a legal form of firework that does not leave the ground, does not explode, and
  meets all state regulations for noise), that includes:
  • Incorporation of 7 percent fee on the sale of ground-based sparkling devices
  in accordance with AB1403 for funding a robust, dangerous firework
  community education and enforcement plan;
  • Incorporate that 4 percent of post-cost revenue be designated to the
  Nonprofit Partnership to support grants for Long Beach community needs,
  determined by the City Council annually; and
  • Incorporate a selection process where 501(c) 3 organizations can apply for
  permits to operate up to 10 stands spread across the city (excluding the
  coastal zone). The application should score for articulation of how the funds
  raised support Long Beach residents. A lottery is being utilized when more
  than 10 applicants are qualify.

  Office or Department:  Cindy Allen, Councilwoman, Second District; Roberto
  Uranga, Vice Mayor, Seventh District; Mary Zendejas,
  Councilwoman, First District

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

  Office or Department:  Roberto Uranga, Vice Mayor, Seventh District, Chair,
  Intergovernmental Affairs Committee

  Suggested Action:  Approve recommendation.

25. 25-56613  Recommendation to request City Attorney to agendize an ordinance to regulate the
  sale and use of CA State Fire Marshall-approved ground-based sparkling devices
  (a legal form of firework that does not leave the ground, does not explode, and
  meets all state regulations for noise), that includes:
  • Incorporation of 7 percent fee on the sale of ground-based sparkling devices
  in accordance with AB1403 for funding a robust, dangerous firework
  community education and enforcement plan;
  • Incorporate that 4 percent of post-cost revenue be designated to the
  Nonprofit Partnership to support grants for Long Beach community needs,
  determined by the City Council annually; and
  • Incorporate a selection process where 501(c) 3 organizations can apply for
  permits to operate up to 10 stands spread across the city (excluding the
  coastal zone). The application should score for articulation of how the funds
  raised support Long Beach residents. A lottery is being utilized when more
  than 10 applicants are qualify.

  A motion was made by Councilwoman Allen, seconded by Vice Mayor
  Uranga, to approve recommendation for the City Manager to work
  with the Fire and Police Departments to prepare a report and return to
  City Council with a recommendation as to whether the City should

  Page 13 of 19
   CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
  TUESDAY, OCTOBER 7, 2025
  411 W. OCEAN BOULEVARD
  CIVIC CHAMBERS, 5:00 PM

adopt an ordinance regarding the potential sale and use within the
City of Long Beach of CA State Fire Marshall-approved ground-based
sparkling devices (a form of firework that does not leave the ground,
does not explode, and meets all state regulations for noise). This
report should include an assessment of revenue options from the sale
of the sparkling devices, including a potential 7 percent fee on the
sale of the devices for funding a robust, dangerous firework
community education and enforcement plan and a 4 percent post-cost
revenue to go to the Nonprofit Partnership to support grants for
community needs as determined by the City Council annually. The
report should consider how many stands would be appropriate for
our city and consider how the stands spread throughout the city
(excluding the coastal zone) could be operated by 501(c)(3)
organizations such that the funds raised by operation of the stands
would have the greatest impact on Long Beach residents. The report
should consider how to determine which nonprofit entities should
receive permits for stands if there are more that apply than the
number of permitted stands, including consideration of a lottery
system. The report should address fire risk associated with these
sparkling devices as well as noise impacts, how other cities are
regulating these sparkling devices, whether a 4 percent post-cost
revenue percentage provided to nonprofits is appropriate or whether
that number should increase, whether the 7 percent fee for an
education and enforcement plan is sufficient to cover all associated
costs, and what the fiscal impact would be on the city from
implementation of this program. The report should include
information as to how the city would track data regarding
enforcement of its fireworks regulations with this change
implemented. The City Manager’s team should review any and all
relevant information, including any information provided by TNT
Fireworks (the manufacturer of the sparkling devices), regarding
these sparkling devices in preparation of the report. The report
should incorporate several restrictions on the use and sale of these
sparkling devices: 1) they will be prohibited (sale and use) in the
coastal zone (including on the beaches) and 2) the PBID and other
BIDs will not be permitted to participate in their sales. City Manager
should return in 60 days with either the completed report or an update
on the progress of preparation of the report and, when the report is
completed, the recommendation regarding an ordinance. The
motion carried by the following vote:
